_comment: LIVE page manifest — the authoritative top-level child count for every page of every
tracked Figma file, measured 2026-08-26. This file and the sibling
<fileKey>__<pageId>.tsv node lists are the ONLY inputs coverage.mjs takes from Figma;
everything else it derives.
★ This SUPERSEDES pages.json's `liveChildren`, which is stale in both directions.
Measured drift on 2026-08-26: Home 2 129 -> 168, Governance 260 -> 331, Home 1 227 ->
254, Coinflip 37 -> 45, Cover Images 24 -> 42, Safari Slots 24 -> 33, Baccarat 19 -> 21,
Roulette 19 -> 21, Scratchers 20 -> 21, Slide 17 -> 18, Wallet 1 179 -> 178, Plinko 22 ->
21, Hi-Lo 20 -> 16. Do not re-derive coverage from pages.json.
METHOD. Counts came from one use_figma call per FILE running:
const out = [];
for (const p of figma.root.children) { await p.loadAsync(); out.push({id:p.id,name:p.name,n:p.children.length}); }
return out;
`page.loadAsync()` was validated against `setCurrentPageAsync` before use: Home 2
reported 168 by BOTH methods, and Play/Social matched their independently-known counts.
That matters because an unloaded page reports `children.length === 0` — a plausible zero,
not an error.
`n` here is the LOUD GUARD: coverage.mjs refuses to run if a page's .tsv does not have
exactly `n` rows. A short file means a chunk was lost to the 20KB tool-output truncation,
and a silently short harvest would report a smaller denominator and a HIGHER completion
percentage — failing in the flattering direction, which is the failure nobody reviews.
`scope` drives the roll-up. Casey's rulings: Governance is HELD (do not build),
Onboarding is a standing exclusion, and the v2 pages SUPERSEDE Home 1 / Wallet 1 /
Trade 1, so v1 frames are not parity targets.
★ THIS FILE IS NO LONGER ONE DATE. Pages are re-harvested individually and each
carries its own `harvestedAt`; the top-level `harvestedAt` is the ORIGINAL sweep and
governs only the rows that have no per-page override. Read the per-page field before
quoting an age.
★ THE 2026-08-26 SWEEP TRUNCATED `name` AT 20 CHARACTERS. Measured on 2026-09-07:
48 of 49 node lists cap every name at 20 chars (1,157 of them on Titles + Emblems
alone); only the blackjack and bingo pages, re-harvested later under commit 9cd5648
'for full titles', carry whole names. Nothing coverage.mjs does joins on the name —
`classify()` only regex-tests it for canvas chrome, and every furniture pattern is
shorter than the cap — so the truncation costs no accuracy there. It DOES make the
column useless for reading a frame back, which is why re-harvests write the full name.
Do not treat a longer name in a re-harvested page as drift against a shorter one here.
★ 2026-09-08 FULL RE-COUNT. Every page of all three tracked files was re-read with the
METHOD below and its live children.length compared to `n`. All 13 pages of
3sSzw1KewMtUbeLAv7uW0r and all 7 of mhF3BkzlTaGiLzJ7kvpmVc matched exactly — including
Governance at 725, which is the number the 09-07 re-harvest pinned. EIGHT pages of
M6r9FEn042UWTQD1zvy6GM did not: Mines 19->21, Coinflip 45->46, Cover Images 42->44,
Safari Slots 33->61, Cosmic Slots 6->50, Vegas fortune 1->85, Gem Slots 11->36, Wild
card 0->1. All eight .tsv node lists were re-harvested in the same pass and `n` moved
with them, so harvest and manifest still agree.
⛔ THE LOUD GUARD CANNOT SEE THIS FAILURE, and that is worth stating plainly, because
the guard is easy to mistake for cover it does not give. coverage.mjs compares the .tsv
row count to `n` — two numbers produced by the SAME harvest. When a page grows in Figma
afterwards, both stay stale together, they agree, and the run is silent while the
denominator is short and the published percentage is high. The guard catches a TRUNCATED
harvest (tsv < n, tool-output loss); it cannot catch a SUPERSEDED one. Only re-reading
Figma catches that, which is why this row exists. Nothing had re-read Skai-Games since
2026-08-26 — thirteen days.
Non-cosmetic bug fixed in the same pass: Home 1, Home 2 and Trade 2 each carried the key
`harvestedAt` TWICE in one object — '2026-09-08' before `pageName` and '2026-09-07' after
`n`, the first added by commit 76af075 on top of one already there. JSON.parse keeps the
LAST, so all three silently read as the OLDER date and the file under-reported its own
freshness on exactly the pages most recently re-harvested. The duplicate is gone; those
three now carry `nVerifiedAt` instead, which says what actually happened to them today —
their child count was re-counted and confirmed, their .tsv was not re-harvested. Do not
read `nVerifiedAt` as a harvest date.
★ `openReports` (added 2026-09-08) is the number of ACTIONABLE bug reports whose own
`figma_link` resolves to this page — every node-id taken from the report's link, then
walked to its PAGE with getNodeByIdAsync, never guessed from a title. 548 of the 599
actionable reports carry a link; 536 resolved, 12 name a node Figma no longer has, 0 could
not be placed. Every page any report cites is in this list and carries a scope, so there
is no unscoped citation left — the one gap was a whole FILE, not a page, and it is in
`fileAliases` above.
⛔ IT IS NOT A SCOPE INPUT. `scope` is Casey's ruling; the count is pressure against it.
193 of the 536 cite a v1-superseded page — Home 1 87, Trade 1 64, Wallet 1 42 — plus 8 on
held Governance, 5 on excluded Onboarding and 1 on wip Vegas fortune.
⛔⛔ RETRACTION, same day. An earlier version of this paragraph called those 193 reports
'filed against frames nobody is meant to build toward' and called a v1-superseded page
'not a parity target at all'. THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong in the dangerous
direction: it reads as permission to close live parity work. `v1-superseded` describes a
FILE DUPLICATION, not a retirement. See _pages.SCOPE-WARNING.md, and do not restore the
earlier reading from this file's git history.
Measured live 2026-09-08 rather than taken on faith, and every number below is a
top-level-child count read off the page itself:
- Portfolio frames:  Home 1 50,  Home 2 0.
- Perps frames:      Trade 1 78, Trade 2 0.
- Spot frames:       Trade 1 124, Trade 2 2.
- Trench frames:     Trade 1 8,  Trade 2 136.
Trade 2 is overwhelmingly a TRENCH surface, not a replacement for Trade 1. For Portfolio,
Perps and Spot the v1 page is the ONLY design that exists, so a report citing a Home 1 or
Trade 1 frame for /portfolio or /spot is citing the only spec there is.
Where the duplication actually shows up, also measured: Home 1 vs Home 2, Wallet 1 vs
Wallet 2 and Trade 1 vs Trade 2 share ZERO top-level ids with each other — they are
different pages, not two versions of one. The copying is ACROSS FILES: pageId 3:3 exists
in both 3sSzw1KewMtUbeLAv7uW0r (tombstone, 154 children) and mhF3BkzlTaGiLzJ7kvpmVc
(v1-superseded, 420), and 144 of the tombstone's 154 ids are present in mhF3. That is
what 'moved to Skai Web App 2' means: copied file-to-file with ids preserved.
So the useful reading of this number is the reverse of the one first written here: 158 of
the 193 were filed in September and 105 are still `new`, which is not a reporting defect
but a live backlog on the only extant spec. Do not close a report on the
`v1-superseded` label alone; check whether the cited surface has a v2 counterpart first.
Deciding the labels is still Casey's call and nothing here changes one.
It is a SNAPSHOT of 2026-09-08 and goes stale as reports are filed and closed. Re-derive
it rather than trusting it if the date matters.
method: use_figma read-only; figma.root.children for the page list, then page.loadAsync() per page for children

fileAliases._why: Report `figma_link`s do not all carry a tracked fileKey. An untracked key resolves to no page and so to no scope, and an unscoped citation is worse than a retired one: nobody can tell whether to build it. Record the mapping here rather than letting each lane rediscover it.

_wrongFileKeyOnReports.note: A report can also carry a TRACKED fileKey that is the wrong one, which reads as a deleted node rather than as a bad link. Because pageIds 2003:674 / 2998:19593 / 3:3 exist in BOTH 3sSzw1KewMtUbeLAv7uW0r and mhF3BkzlTaGiLzJ7kvpmVc, and 144 of the 154 ids on the 3sSzw `3:3` tombstone are also present in mhF3, a node deleted from the 3sSzw copy is often still alive in mhF3. Before calling a cited node deleted, look for it in the SIBLING file. 12 reports cited a node absent from the file their link named; re-checked against mhF3, 3 of the 12 are alive there and only 9 are genuinely absent from both.
